principle: US material superiority is large but finite. Replenishment, CAP/search, ASW, damaged-carrier escort, close gunfire, UDT/channel work and island suppression consume overlapping deck/escort/command capacity.

4Feb.CVE_close_support_note: Six CVE support groups primarily cover CAP/ASW/spotting and preliminary-islet work; only bounded strike sorties are counted as direct suppression, not free additions to TF58 totals.
4Feb.old_battleship_support: Seven existing old-battleship support slots remain available in the assault package; they begin deliberate target-system reduction and channel/islet preparation. No new upstream loss is introduced.
4Feb.fast_battleships: Most remain with TF58/anti-surface cover during the morning. By evening, increased confidence that the Japanese carrier force is retiring permits 1-2 fast-BB-class hulls to shift toward intermediate covering geometry, not close beach bombardment.
4Feb.destroyer_tradeoff: Additional close-fire/UDT/islet slots are created by moving some DDs inward; DE/CVE air partially backfill ASW, but the outer screen is not simultaneously at maximum density.
4Feb.result: Suppression rises from the 3-Feb recovery day but remains below a theoretical all-deck maximum because carrier air groups and decks are still absorbing 2-Feb losses/cross-deck congestion.

5Feb.CVE_and_gunfire: Close-support CVEs, old battleships, cruisers and destroyers shift from broad suppression toward repeated reattack of target systems, flanking-islet support, artillery-observation preparation and lagoon approaches.
5Feb.bombardment_learning: Tarawa-derived doctrine is already present in historical FLINTLOCK-type planning; this branch adds persistence and reattack rather than another linear 2-3x multiplier. Smoke, dust, target identification and fire-sector conflicts cap useful rate.
5Feb.traffic_congestion: More LVT/LST/LCI and engineer reserve improves resilience but causes intermittent staging/lagoon-lane congestion during preliminary moves. Commanders separate gunfire, UDT and assault-lane windows rather than simply pushing all craft forward at once.
5Feb.result: By late 5-Feb the US has completed a strong but not magically perfect preparation cycle. Remaining Japanese positions are suppressed unevenly rather than erased.

anti_double_count: Do not count CAP/search/ASW sorties as island-suppression sorties.
Do not add Cabot survivor aircraft as an extra flight deck.
Do not count fast battleships as both carrier screen and close bombardment in the same time block.
Do not turn additional bombardment ammunition into a linear lethality multiplier.
